title: Simple Staining

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: To visualize basic cell shape, size, and arrangement using a single stain, without differentiating cell wall type.
principle: A single basic dye (positively charged) is attracted to the negatively charged bacterial cell surface, coloring all cells uniformly regardless of Gram type.
requiredReagents: Methylene blue, crystal violet, or safranin (a single basic dye)

procedure.instruction: Prepare a thin smear on a clean slide and air dry.
Flood the smear with the chosen stain for the time appropriate to that dye (e.g. methylene blue ~1 minute).
Rinse gently with water and blot dry.

observations: All cells appear a single color; record shape (coccus, bacillus, spirillum) and arrangement (diplo-, strepto-, staphylo-, etc.).
interpretation: Simple staining confirms morphology and arrangement only — it provides no Gram-reaction or biochemical information.
precautions: Treat all specimens as potentially infectious.
Avoid excess heat during fixation, which distorts cell shape.
limitations: Cannot distinguish Gram-positive from Gram-negative organisms.
Does not reveal internal structures without a specialized stain (e.g. spore or capsule stains).
biosafetyNotes: Biosafety level depends on the organism, not the staining method.
